public_rationale: Marcus said we did not yet have AI that is flexible, general and as reliable as a human. In the period before the post, the most prominent system, ChatGPT, was described by OpenAI itself as sometimes writing 'plausible-sounding but incorrect or nonsensical answers'. OpenAI's CEO said it was not for reliable factual answers. That is far below human-level reliability. In February 2023 OpenAI still described AGI as not yet created (context). No credible claim that AGI existed at the time was found.
limitations: The evidence is developer admissions rather than a formal test of the AGI definition.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: We do not yet have AI as flexible and reliable as AGI.

statement.document_title: AGI will not happen in your lifetime. Or will it?

from_speaker: flexible and general, with resourcefulness and reliability comparable to (or beyond) human intelligence
our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of January 2023, no AI system met Marcus's stated AGI definition, meaning flexible and general intelligence with resourcefulness and reliability comparable to humans.
The target period runs from the ChatGPT launch (30 November 2022) to the post date. That was the latest state of AI public evidence could report on.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence from the period that even the most prominent AI systems had basic reliability limits far below human level, with no credible claim that AGI had been achieved.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence that some AI system at the time met the stated standard of human-comparable flexibility, resourcefulness and reliability.
